The package fails on three points; everything else checked out.

perf_ok is false only because of problem 3. perf.sh itself is within budget on every corpus file in both runs, with quality columns identical to 3abbfeb. The slowdown is on inputs that take the new `rest_sizes` path, which perf.sh's corpus does not contain.

Suggested direction for the fix round:
- Bars: give every block proxy whose box feeds a bar's fit its static frame (a member of a branched composite as well as a direct branch), and make the `!same_graph` fallback agree with route(). Bound the cost at the same time, for example a size cap with a documented fallback or a memo of the static frame, and report route() timings on a fork-to-block input.
- Class: do not keep a stray redraw that costs more than the drawing it replaces, or that leaves the strays as curves; add a regression test on a 24-30 source labelled, carded LR fan-in.
- Docs: correct the "no other class diagram draws differently" claim.

Limits of my checks:
- My pick check samples a B-spline through the waypoints rather than the painter's path, so it reports misses on invisible links, hops and explicit curves. Those lists are identical on 3abbfeb; the in-repo painted-stroke picking test passes.
- The implementer's known open case (a choice dragged toward its targets leaves a label over a sibling stroke) I did not re-test; the new tests drag across the flow only.

Housekeeping: the repo was not modified and `git status` in the worktree is clean. I removed my 3abbfeb worktree (verify/c-leftovers/pre); the two small harness target directories (about 100 MB together) remain, and 8.2 GB is free. perf.sh and render.sh are not executable, so I ran them through `bash`.

fix:c-leftovers#1.summary:
All five review findings are fixed in two new commits on `ccr-ccc6d89a-5cxd7e-par`; guard was ALL GREEN before each, nothing pushed, nothing amended. The quiet-window timing rule could not be met: the other track kept the load at 1–3 throughout, so timings are alternated runs under load.

**1. Bars under drag (blocking).** Every builder now draws the static bar.
- `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-flowmaid/cac93b13-7009-5470-94b5-477c61df0333/scratchpad/verify/c-leftovers/in/s7_bar_outer_holds_block.mmd`, `d` +250: scene, `route_partial`, `route` and `route_sized` all give 335x8 (was 460 in the last two).
- x7 with an edited label: `route_partial` on the stale base and `route()` both give 321x8 (was 446 vs 321).
- Cause fixed as you diagnosed: `rest_sizes` now uses the new `scene::bar_branches`, which walks the same spans as `fit_bars`. `compound::route_partial` fits the rest's bars the way `route` does instead of copying them from `base`.
- Sweep: 146 state diagrams with bars, drags through `route`, `route_sized`, `route_partial` and the drag back — no bar differs from the static one (369 did at 3abbfeb).
- One case left as it was: a block none of whose nodes moved is still returned as `base` drew it, so with a stale base a bar inside that block keeps the old length (three checks on `s5_bar_nested_block`). That is the existing unmoved-part shortcut; it is documented in the code but not in the CHANGELOG.

**2. Class fan regression (blocking).** The real cause was not the `usize::MAX` acceptance. When a group holding a curve found no drawing, the routes' usual stacking was skipped altogether.
- `nest_jogs` now retries from the laid-out routes with that curve left alone. A curve group is accepted only if it costs less than keeping the curve (new `curve_cost`).
- Against 3abbfeb on your 2,784 fans (scene, route, two drags): 96 drawings better, 0 worse.
- 26 inputs return byte-identical to 3abbfeb, including all the ones you named and `aa81d3da`; nothing else differs from 842051c across 6,378 class inputs.
- The wide LR fans keep their two outer curves, exactly as before the package.

**3. Drag budget (blocking).** The block's static frame is now memoised per thread, keyed by the block's whole part graph, sizes and labels, capped at 32 blocks; `scene()` fills it. Only the first `route()` of a graph no `scene()` has laid out pays for the layout, once.

| input | 3abbfeb | 2e5dacd | now |
|---|---|---|---|
| t1, 60 states, `route()` ms | 2.9–3.1 | 7.2–8.6 | 3.0–3.2 |
| t2, 25 states | 0.58–0.68 | 1.57–1.67 | 0.59–0.62 |
| t3, four blocks | 0.34 | 0.93–1.03 | 0.34–0.39 |
| t4, 120 states | 11.6–11.7 | 31–32 | 11.7–11.9 |
| x7 | 0.036–0.040 | 0.07 | 0.037–0.042 |
| r0_y2_state_nested | 0.64–0.75 | 1.32–1.42 | 0.64–0.71 |

- `route_partial` is unchanged within noise (t4 3.8–4.9 vs 4.3–5.8).
- The memo key needed equality on graphs, so `model::Graph`, `Node`, `Edge`, `Subgraph` and `SubEdge` now derive `PartialEq` — an additive public API change, listed in the CHANGELOG.

**4 and 5 (docs).** The CHANGELOG now gives the real class counts and says what a curve without a place keeps. `o.A` names (also `class o.A`, `o.A : +x int`) are documented in CHANGELOG and README and tested; I confirmed mermaid 12.2.0 rejects them.

**Output.** 4,846 flowchart and state inputs (scene, route, three drags by `route` and `route_partial`) are byte-identical to 3abbfeb except four state diagrams whose bars a drag used to stretch. The 25-diagram corpus is byte-identical to the before render. No snapshot or gate changed.

**Performance notes.**
- The one `perf.sh` run (`bash …/perf.sh`, the script is not executable) and four before/after pairs of the quality example on the flowchart corpus were noisy and disagreed with each other.
- Six alternated best-of rounds on dense-lr, dense-td and bench-75 overlap completely between 3abbfeb and now, and four more rounds on seven other corpus files match in route, scene and partial.
- Class timings on seven inputs, measured before the final `curve_cost` tweak and not re-timed, stay within budget: at most +0.7 ms (4.36 → 4.9 ms on the 24-fan); the fan of six goes 0.29 → 0.42 ms.

**Housekeeping.**
- db4d89b's message mis-splits the 26 restored inputs; 3b6c08b's message corrects it (15 had measured worse, 11 had changed without a measured difference).
- Scratch harness and results are in `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-flowmaid/cac93b13-7009-5470-94b5-477c61df0333/scratchpad/clfix`; I deleted my own `clfix/pre/target` and `clfix/pkg-target` build directories there.

Cause of the above, confirmed with an instrumented scratch copy: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-flowmaid/cac93b13-7009-5470-94b5-477c61df0333/scratchpad/wt/par/src/class.rs:552 `loop_faces` ranks sharings by `(hits, near, pref)` (line 619). `hits` adds 1 per face region that meets a box (line 614) or per end on the face (line 590), however many loops go through. For TB_b5 the default split costs (1, 2, 14) — label chips within LOOP_CLEAR of C — and all five on one face costs (1, 0, 30) — loops through C. Equal hits, so `near` picks the deep stack. The search is also entered now whenever near > 0 (line 624), where before a default with 0 hits was kept. The doc comment (class.rs:549) and CHANGELOG.md:211-212 say 'no loop is sent into a box to spare a neighbour's loop'; that is false.
